agree.reason: Long-tenured staff who don't want phone work get facts and empathy, but nothing that lowers the risk of saying yes: no $1.50 raise, no seniority-based shift choice, no 6-month severance safety net, so many will start looking elsewhere.

honest.reason: It correctly drops the 'better for everyone' claim and states the brief's numbers accurately, though 'get it right the first time' and the strain on phone staff are mild unsupported additions.

works_the_facts.reason: The figures are only repeated and never worked: no severance example for a ten-year employee (20 weeks), no concrete pay increase, and no point about what the 9-minute wait does if nothing changes.

right_comparison.reason: It shows the falling branch visits against rising phone and chat demand, which explains why keeping the branches isn't realistic, but for staff it frames the choice as the center versus severance without saying that closure is fixed and 9-to-5 hours aren't available anywhere.

qualification.reason: The offer date, decision deadline and Q&A are left as [date] placeholders when Feb 14 and March 1 were available, and nothing says what happens if the deadline passes.

objections.reason: The dislike of phone work and rotating hours is acknowledged but not answered, even though the seniority shift choice and the 6-month option to still take severance would meet it directly, and the two weeks of rumours go unmentioned.

fit.reason: It is a COO email of roughly the right length and structure, but leftover placeholders for the name, dates, HR contact and an editorial note mean it can't be sent as written.
